name: Dubai chocolate
blurb: A pistachio-and-knafeh chocolate bar from Dubai that TikTok turned into a global craze
title: Dubai Chocolate Meaning: The Viral TikTok Pistachio Bar
description: Dubai chocolate is a milk chocolate bar filled with crunchy shredded pastry and pistachio cream, made famous by a December 2023 TikTok of a Fix Dessert Chocolatier bar.
answer: Dubai chocolate is a thick milk chocolate bar filled with crispy shredded filo pastry (kadayif) and a pistachio-tahini cream, a chocolate version of the Middle Eastern dessert knafeh. It comes from Fix Dessert Chocolatier in Dubai, whose bar "Can't Get Knafeh of It" went viral after creator Maria Vehera filmed herself eating it in a TikTok in December 2023. The crunchy, green-filled cross-section made it a 2024–25 food trend copied by big brands, bakeries and home cooks worldwide.

sections.h: What it is and where it comes from
body: The original bar was created by Sarah Hamouda, a British-Egyptian engineer living in Dubai, with chef Nouel Catis Omamalin; Hamouda runs Fix with her husband Yezen Alani. It went on sale around 2021–2022 in small batches. The point of every video is the snap: breaking the bar open shows a bright green pistachio filling and you hear the pastry crunch.

body.note: "Dubai chocolate" is a nickname, not a brand. The viral video never used the phrase; it named the Fix bars. Today the name covers any pistachio-and-kadayif chocolate, wherever it is made.

head: Date
Event
rows: Fix Dessert Chocolatier develops and starts selling "Can't Get Knafeh of It" in Dubai.
Maria Vehera posts her TikTok trying three Fix bars; it gathers tens of millions of views and Fix orders jump from six a day to about 100 a minute.
The trend spreads on TikTok; copycat recipes and bakery versions appear in Europe, Asia and the US.
A Cologne court orders Aldi to stop selling a "Dubai" chocolate made in Turkey, part of a dispute over the name.
Lindt and other big makers sell their own versions; UK supermarket Waitrose limits shoppers to two bars; the craze is linked to a global pistachio shortage.
Spin-offs keep coming, such as a chewy Dubai chocolate cookie that goes viral in South Korea.

ul: Taste tests: "Rating every Dubai chocolate from the supermarket, the crunch is everything."
Recipes: "Homemade Dubai chocolate with toasted kataifi and pistachio cream."
As a label for anything pistachio-green: "Dubai chocolate latte", "Dubai chocolate strawberries".
Joking about the hype: "Paid how much for one bar? It's just a very expensive candy bar with pistachios."

body: The peak was 2024–2025, but Dubai chocolate has settled in as a regular flavour in shops and cafes. The trend now lives on through new mash-ups rather than the original bar. Some criticism follows it too: a German food-safety study in Baden-Württemberg found problems in all eight samples it tested, so buy from sellers you trust. Like Labubu, it is a product that became a meme.

faq.a: Milk chocolate around a filling of toasted shredded filo pastry (kadayif or kataifi) mixed with pistachio cream and tahini.
Fix Dessert Chocolatier in Dubai, founded by Sarah Hamouda; she created the bar with chef Nouel Catis Omamalin.

faq.q: Why did Dubai chocolate go viral?
faq.a: A December 2023 TikTok showed the satisfying crunch and green filling, and the video racked up tens of millions of views within months.
